_oq_discrepancy.text: Treat rate: the only dose is 4.2% with 10.3% HiTEC® 12200 to reach HiTEC® 12204L performance (12204L itself: 14.2% wt). The basis of the 4.2% is not printed, and 10.3% + 4.2% = 14.5% differs from the 14.2% 12204L rate; recorded as printed, not reconciled. Confirm with Afton.

Older Afton editions retrieved from the Internet Archive (original bytes, not cited as sources): PDS 07/11 (http://www.aftonchemical.com/ProductDataSheets/Engine%20Oil/HiTEC-5748_PDS.pdf, snapshot 2012-05-03, SHA-256 ee8581a8...); PDS 03/18 (HiTEC-5748_PDS_1.pdf, snapshot 2023-02-02, identical to the 2019-07-13 capture, SHA-256 3bfb7f0d...); PDS 04/21 (HiTEC-5748_PDS_2.pdf, snapshot 2023-01-28, SHA-256 f291807c...). Typical characteristics differ between editions (edition differences on properties without a template field): 07/11 Specific Gravity 0.865, Flash Point (PMCC) 155 min., Viscosity @ 40°C 15000 cSt, Viscosity @ 100°C 1140 cSt, Color 5.0 max.; 03/18 0.855, 135 min., 1100 cSt @ 100°C, Color 5.0 max., Thickening Power @ 100°C 6.55; 04/21 and 05/23 0.855, 135 min., 1100 cSt @ 100°C, Color 3.0 max., Dilute Viscosity @ 100°C 11.55 cSt. The recommended dosage table is identical in all four editions. The record uses the 05/23 edition.

SSI discrepancy, not reconciled: Afton's HiTEC 5748 PDS prints 'Shear Stability Index %: 22' (05/23 and 04/21) and 'a typical Shear Stability Index (SSI) of 22' (03/18); the 07/11 edition says 'It is based on 23 SSI polymer' (base-polymer basis); Afton's HiTEC 12360 bulletin DL2-13692.pdf (07/20, p.2) describes 'HiTEC® 5748 25SSI OCP' / '25SSI viscosity modifier'. None of these documents prints the SSI test method, cycle count or base oil, so comparability is not established and no conflict entry is recorded. Confirm the SSI and its method with Afton.

Storage temperature differs between Richful documents (no template field; recorded here, not resolved): TDS DL2-14874.pdf p.1 (undated; PDF created 2021-05-16): 'For short-term storage and transportation, the temperature of the product shall not surpass 75℃; for long-term storage,it shall not surpass 45℃.' Richful product page https://www.richful.com/catalogueDetail.html?id=105 (English; Chinese id=104), page data feed productId=105, record created 2023-05-23, no revision date, retrieved 2026-10-23: 'The maximum storage and transportation temperature shall not exceed 60℃ in short term, and shall not exceed 45℃ in long term.' (Chinese page: '短期最高温度不应超过 60℃；长期储存最高温度不应超过 45℃'). Both state the same condition (short-term storage and transport) and the same 45℃ long-term limit, so the short-term limits genuinely differ (75℃ vs 60℃). The page is reachable directly but is not in Richful's public catalogue listing. Confirm the current short-term limit with Richful.

Claims printed for the equivalent route only: DL2-14639.pdf p.2 (08/18) marks API SL, API SJ and DDC 93K214 in the row '10.3%¹ | 4.2% HiTEC® 12250 | SAE 15W-40 | GP II'. MAN 3275: the PDS footnote reads '*:Equivalent performance. MAN 3275 now obsolete' (claim_type 'other'); DL2-14639.pdf footnote 5 for the equivalent route reads 'Meets requirements of (MRO)'. The wordings differ but do not contradict each other; not recorded as a conflict.

MB 228.3 approval scope is route-specific (not recorded as a conflict): the PDS (06/17, p.2) marks MB 228.3 'p' ('p: MB package approval') in the row 'API CI-4 Plus | SAE 15W40 | HiTEC® 12204L @ 14.2%', i.e. for HiTEC® 12204L used alone. DL2-14639.pdf (08/18, p.2) shows a plain dot, without 'P' ('MB Package Approval', used in other rows), in the MB 228.3 column of the row '10.3%¹ | 4.2% HiTEC® 12250 | SAE 15W-40 | GP II', i.e. for the two-product combination HiTEC® 12200 + HiTEC® 12250. Footnote 1 ('14.2% HiTEC® 12204L = 10.3% HiTEC® 12200 + 4.2% HiTEC® 12250') and the PDS sentence ('The performance level of HiTEC® 12204L can also be achieved...') state equivalent composition or performance, not identical approval status; the two markings describe different formulation routes and are not shown to contradict each other. Confirm with Afton whether the MB package approval also covers the HiTEC 12200 + 12250 route.
